statement: 4 We presented a pseudopolynomial-time algorithm for MCKP with running time O(n + wmax ), based on upper-hull greedy anchors, a proximity bound, and a subset-sum separation argument. The same dynamic program also yields optimal values for wmax + 1 consecutive capacities. This windowed viewpoint leads to applications in bounded-domain (max, +) convolution, including deterministic network calculus. For instances with small price ranges, the same approach yields a symmetric bound of O(n + p4max ). An open problem is to match the best known small-item bounds for 0-1 Knapsack and improve the dependence on wmax or pmax for MCKP. For 0-1 Knapsack, stronger bounds in the small-item regime rely on refined additive-combinatorial tools that exploit unrestricted mixing of items. These techniques do not transfer cleanly to MCKP: the class constraint prevents arbitrary combinations and breaks the additive structure that those methods use. Closing this gap remains open. In 3 particular, the O(n + wmax ) bound for 0-1 Knapsack from [11] relies on structural properties of unrestricted item sets and does not seem to extend to the class-constrained setting.
